Case_23002/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: The microscopic pathological study of the liver biopsy tissue found dense eosinophilic infiltration with Charcot-Laden crystals

description.short_caption: Histopathology of liver biopsy showing dense eosinophilic infiltration with Charcot-Laden crystals.
description.detailed_description: This histopathological image shows a liver biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The tissue demonstrates dense infiltration of eosinophils, identifiable by their bright eosinophilic (pink) cytoplasm. Charcot-Laden crystals, which are elongated and refractile structures, are visible among the infiltrating cells. These findings are consistent with eosinophilic inflammation, which may be associated with parasitic infections, drug reactions, or other causes of eosinophilia.
